header.quote: An X-Signature header containing the request signature.

scheme.value: HMAC-SHA256, lowercase hex digest (the page says HMAC hex digest; sha256 is shown in the Node example createHmac call)
scheme.quote: Lemon Squeezy generates the hash using an HMAC hex digest

scheme_sha256_evidence.value: Node example builds the HMAC with sha256 and a hex digest

signed_content.value: The request payload (raw body) only; no timestamp or other fields are included
signed_content.quote: Lemon Squeezy will use the signing secret to generate a hash of the payload and send the hash in the X-Signature header of the request.

header_format.value: The header value is the bare hex digest, no prefix and no key=value pairs; a single signature (the Node example compares the whole header value to the computed hex digest)

secret_source.value: A signing secret you choose yourself when creating the webhook, usually a random string of 6 to 40 characters; it is not generated by Lemon Squeezy
secret_source.quote: The secret can be anything you want but is normally a random string between 6 and 40 characters in length.
secret_source.short: A signing secret you choose (6 to 40 characters)

secret_scope.value: Per webhook (each webhook has its own callback URL, signing secret and event list)
secret_scope.quote: This is a secret (usually a random string) between 6 and 40 characters that will be used to sign each request.

timestamp_tolerance.value: not stated by the provider (no timestamp header or replay window is documented)

raw_body_note.value: No prose about raw bodies; the Node example hashes request.rawBody and compares with crypto.timingSafeEqual

constant_time_compare.value: The docs example uses crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length Buffers

node.value: none found: the official JavaScript SDK (github.com/lmsqueezy/lemonsqueezy.js) exposes webhook management functions (listWebhooks, createWebhook, updateWebhook, getWebhook, deleteWebhook) and its src/webhooks folder holds only those; no signature verification helper seen

docs_examples_languages.value: The signing page shows hand-written verification examples in Node, PHP, Python (Django) and Ruby (Rails)

method_and_content_type.value: POST, Content-Type application/json; the body is a JSON:API resource object
method_and_content_type.quote: A Content-Type header set to application/json.

event_type_location.value: Header X-Event-Name, and body path meta.event_name
event_type_location.quote: An X-Event-Name header with the name of the event that triggered the webhook.
event_type_location.short: X-Event-Name header, and meta.event_name in the body

event_type_in_body.value: meta.event_name in the JSON body (example: order_created)

custom_data.value: meta.custom_data holds custom data passed through checkout; present for Order, Subscription and License key related events
custom_data.quote: you will find a custom_data object inside the meta field for all Order, Subscription and License key related events.

delivery_id.value: not stated by the provider (no delivery-id header; data.id is the resource ID, for example the order, not the delivery)

handshake.value: not stated by the provider (no ping or challenge on setup)

batching.value: One resource object per request (order, subscription, subscription invoice, license key, customer or affiliate object depending on event)
batching.quote: The webhook body will be a JSON:API resource object that relates to the event

https_certificate.value: For HTTPS URLs the SSL certificate is verified before sending
https_certificate.quote: the SSL certificate of the URL will be verified before sending the request.

success_status.quote: Return a 200 response to show that the webhook was successfully captured.

retries.value: Any non-200 response is retried up to three more times with exponential backoff (example given: 5 secs, 25 secs, 125 secs), after which the request is considered failed and is no longer retried
retries.quote: the webhook will be retried up to three more times using an exponential backoff strategy (e.g. 5 secs, 25 secs, 125 secs)
retries.short: Up to three more times with back-off (for example 5 s, 25 s, 125 s)

retries_end.value: After the last retry the request is considered failed
retries_end.quote: at which point the request will be considered failed and will no longer be retried.

disabling.value: not stated by the provider (no automatic disabling is documented)

duplicates.value: not stated by the provider (a retry resends after any non-200 answer)
duplicates.quote: If the response status is anything else, the webhook will be retried

all_event_names.quote: This is the full list of webhook events available in Lemon Squeezy.

common.meaning: A new order was placed; data is an order object
common.quote: Occurs when a new order is successfully placed.

common.meaning: Full or partial refund on an order
common.quote: Occurs when a full or partial refund is made on an order.

common.meaning: New subscription; always accompanied by order_created
common.quote: Occurs when a new subscription is successfully created.

common.meaning: Catch-all for any change to a subscription
common.quote: This event can be used as a “catch-all” to make sure you always have access to the latest subscription data.

common.meaning: Cancelled by customer or store owner; enters a grace period until the next billing date
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription is cancelled manually by the customer or store owner.

common.meaning: Cancelled subscription ended, or dunning completed for a past_due subscription
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription has ended after being previously cancelled, or once dunning has been completed for past_due subscriptions.

common.meaning: A subscription payment succeeded; data is a subscription invoice object
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription payment is successful.
Occurs when a subscription renewal payment fails.

common.meaning: A successful payment after a failed one; sent alongside subscription_payment_success
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription has a successful payment after a failed payment.

common.meaning: License key created from a new order; sent alongside order_created
common.quote: Occurs when a license key is created from a new order.

recommended_minimum.quote: We suggest subscribing to these events as a minimum so that your application will have the latest data.

where_url_is_entered.value: Dashboard Settings » Webhooks (app.lemonsqueezy.com/settings/webhooks), or the Lemon Squeezy API; a webhook needs a callback URL, a signing secret and a list of events
where_url_is_entered.quote: Webhooks can be set up and managed from Settings » Webhooks in your dashboard or programatically using the Lemon Squeezy API.

test_mode.value: In test mode Lemon Squeezy sends webhooks for events in the test mode store just like live mode; test and live webhooks are kept separate
test_mode.quote: Test and live mode webhooks are kept separate within your account, meaning a test mode webhook will only be triggered for test mode data and vice versa.

test_tools.value: Simulate webhook events: from the Lemon Squeezy admin, choose an event and send it manually for any test mode order or subscription. Simulatable: subscription_created, subscription_updated, subscription_cancelled, subscription_resumed, subscription_expired, subscription_paused, subscription_unpaused, subscription_plan_changed, order_created, order_refunded.
test_tools.quote: you can simulate webhook events for any test mode order or subscription.

resend_and_log.value: The webhooks settings page logs recent webhooks with event names and full payloads and lets you resend webhooks
resend_and_log.quote: You can see which events have been sent, the full payloads of each request and also resend webhooks if you need to.

api_webhook_object.value: The API webhook object has url, events, last_sent_at and test_mode attributes
api_webhook_object.quote: A boolean indicating if the object was created within test mode.

gotchas.value: order_created is always sent alongside subscription_created
gotchas.quote: An order_created event will always be sent alongside a subscription_created event.

gotchas.value: subscription_payment_success is always sent alongside subscription_payment_recovered
gotchas.quote: A subscription_payment_success event will always be sent alongside a subscription_payment_recovered event.

gotchas.value: order_created is always sent alongside license_key_created (so one purchase delivers several events)
gotchas.quote: An order_created event will always be sent alongside a license_key_created event.

gotchas.value: subscription_updated fires on every subscription event after the initial payment, so granular subscription events are usually redundant if subscription_updated is handled
gotchas.quote: subscription_updated is fired at every event after the initial payment.

gotchas.value: Cancelled subscriptions enter a grace period and can be resumed before expiry
gotchas.quote: The subscription enters a “grace period” until the next billing date, when it will expire.

gotchas.value: custom_data appears in meta only on Order, Subscription and License key related events
gotchas.quote: for all Order, Subscription and License key related events.

gotchas.value: Only a 200 response counts as success; any other status (including other 2xx) triggers a retry
gotchas.quote: If the response status is anything else, the webhook will be retried up to three more times

conflicts.note: The simulate page lists subscription_plan_changed as a simulatable event; the event types page (full list) does not list it.

sources.quote: This is the full list of webhook events available in Lemon Squeezy.
